title: India Beat Afghanistan by an Innings and 300 Runs. It Is the Biggest Test Victory in Their History.
excerpt: Fourteen wickets fell on the third morning. Suthar took seven in the match on debut. Gill's India broke a record that had stood since Rajkot 2018.
body:
It took three days. Fourteen Afghan wickets fell on the final morning alone. When Kuldeep Yadav removed Mohammad Saleem and Nangeyalia Kharote off consecutive deliveries, India had won the one-off Test against Afghanistan by an innings and 300 runs — the largest victory in their 93-year Test history.

The margin surpassed the previous record of an innings and 272 runs against West Indies at Rajkot in 2018. It was, in every sense, a mismatch. But records are records, and this one will stand in the books alongside India's most dominant days.

## How India Got Here

https://x.com/BCCI/status/2063946543712124930

Shubman Gill won the toss and chose to bat at the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium in Mullanpur, New Chandigarh. India's batting line-up did the rest.

KL Rahul scored exactly 100 — the third consecutive Test in which he has been dismissed on that precise score, a quirk of cricketing fate that no Indian batter has experienced before. Gill himself struck 126, adding to his growing collection of WTC centuries (more than any Indian in history). Washington Sundar contributed 52, Rishabh Pant — playing his 50th Test, three years after the car crash that nearly ended his career — chipped in with useful runs, and India declared on 564 for 8 after 127 overs.

Afghanistan, in their own first innings, never had a foothold.

## The Suthar Show

Debutant Manav Suthar was the story of the match. The 23-year-old left-arm spinner from Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan, finished with 6 for 33 in the first innings — figures that made him only the tenth Indian to take a five-wicket haul on Test debut. He joined a list that includes Ravichandran Ashwin, Mohammed Shami, and the legendary Narendra Hirwani.

x-official:https://x.com/BCCI/status/2063931803019382927

"It has been my dream from the very beginning to play for India and to play Test cricket," Suthar said at the post-match presentation, where he was named Player of the Match. "Honestly, it felt quite unreal."

Suthar's accuracy troubled every Afghan batter. He bowled stump to stump, varied his pace when the wicket slowed, and kept his stock ball as his primary weapon. Afghanistan captain Hashmatullah Shahidi was blunt in his assessment: "He was really disciplined. That's why we struggled."

## The Follow-On and Collapse

Afghanistan were bowled out for 152 in their first innings, with Rahmat Shah's composed 60 the lone resistance. Gill enforced the follow-on immediately.

In the second innings, the collapse was faster and more complete. Washington Sundar led the attack with 4 for 36, while Kuldeep Yadav claimed 3 for 30 — including the dramatic back-to-back dismissals of Kharote and Saleem that sealed the match. Sediqullah Atal fought hardest with 42, and Rahmanullah Gurbaz counter-attacked briefly for 24, but the outcome was never in doubt.

Afghanistan were bowled out for 112 in 35.5 overs. The entire match lasted barely into the third afternoon.

## The Bigger Picture

This was India's second Test against Afghanistan, and the scoreline was identical in character to the first — at Bengaluru in 2018, India had won by an innings and 262 runs, also inside three days. For Afghanistan, the gap between their admirable ODI and T20I cricket and the demands of the longest format remains vast.

For India, the victory cements their home dominance and gives Gill a perfect start as full-time Test captain. The spin trio of Suthar, Sundar, and Kuldeep shared 14 wickets in the match, offering Gill the kind of options that Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma built their home records upon.

## Brief Scores

**India:** 564/8 declared (Gill 126, KL Rahul 100, Sundar 52; Saleem 6/175)

**Afghanistan 1st innings:** 152 all out (Rahmat Shah 60; Suthar 6/33)

**Afghanistan 2nd innings:** 112 all out (Atal 42; Sundar 4/36, Kuldeep 3/30)

**Result:** India won by an innings and 300 runs

**Player of the Match:** Manav Suthar
